name: Empty tree
why: An empty tree breaks no rule: True.

name: Wrong child
why: 4 is the right child of 5 but smaller than 5: False.

name: Wrong grandchild
why: Each node is fine next to its own children, but 3 sits in the right subtree of 5 and is smaller than 5: False. Checking only parent against child misses this. Pass down the range of values each subtree may hold.

name: Equal keys
why: Keys must be different: left smaller, right bigger, strictly. False.

name: Too big on the left
why: 12 is in the left subtree of 10 but bigger than 10: False.

name: Negative keys
why: A true search tree: True. If you got False, your starting range may begin at 0 or -1. Use None, or float('inf') and -float('inf'), for 'no limit'.

name: Huge keys
why: True. A starting range like ±10⁹ is too narrow.

name: 100,000 nodes, two keys swapped
expr: (lambda r: (lambda ns: (lambda x, y: [setattr(ns[7_000], 'value', y), setattr(ns[7_001], 'value', x), is_bst(r)][2])(ns[7_000].value, ns[7_001].value))(tnodes(r)))(bst(args[0]))
show: the same tree, with the 7,000th and 7,001st smallest keys swapped
why: False. Somewhere deep in the tree two neighbouring keys are in the wrong order. A full check of ranges (or of the in-order sequence) finds it.
